## Obligation detail

### OBL-001 — Education-record disclosure consent and use limitation

| Field              | Value                                                                                          |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Source             | U.S. Department of Education (SRC-002)                                                         |
| Authority type     | regulation                                                                                     |
| Citation           | 34 CFR 99.30, 99.31(a)(1)                                                                      |
| Locator            | https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CFR-2025-title34-vol1/pdf/CFR-2025-title34-vol1-part99.pdf |
| Source version     | CFR annual edition revised 2025-07-01                                                          |
| Verified on        | 2026-08-19                                                                                     |
| Jurisdiction       | US-FEDERAL                                                                                     |
| Applicability      | APPLIES-AT-PILOT                                                                               |
| Trigger            | A district discloses real education records to SSLS under the school-official exception.       |
| Control family     | PRIVACY                                                                                        |
| Control status     | NOT-APPLICABLE                                                                                 |
| Evidence status    | NOT-PRODUCED                                                                                   |
| Owning route       | Deferred to the work package that first proposes district data ingestion                       |
| Review requirement | LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED                                                                          |
| Review trigger     | Before any district data-sharing agreement is signed                                           |

**What the source states.** 34 CFR 99.31(a)(1) states the conditions of the school-official exception. The regulation addresses the institution's disclosure, not vendor conduct in the abstract.

**Obligation.** A vendor receiving education records under the school-official exception must be under the institution's direct control regarding use and maintenance, use the data only for the authorised purpose, and not re-disclose without authority.

**SSLS interpretation.** SSLS reads this as requiring purpose-bound processing, no secondary use, and contractual re-disclosure control before any real education record is accepted.

**Current phase.** Not triggered. SSLS holds no education records and has no district customer.

**Future phase.** On first district data-sharing agreement, SSLS becomes a party acting for the institution and inherits use and re-disclosure limits.

**Required control.** Purpose-bound data handling, documented direct-control terms, and enforced re-disclosure prohibition.

**Current control.** Zero-PII boundary: synthetic fixtures only, no persistence layer, no ingestion path.

**Evidence required.** Executed data-sharing agreement, purpose-binding design record, re-disclosure control evidence. Minimum method: Contract artifact plus reviewed design record; automated evidence is insufficient.

**Claim permitted.** SSLS may state only that it currently processes no education records.

**Claim refused.** FERPA compliant; FERPA ready; FERPA aligned

**Note.** The zero-PII boundary is what makes this NOT-APPLICABLE. The boundary is therefore a governed control, not an incidental fact.

### OBL-002 — Parental inspection and amendment of education records

| Field              | Value                                                                                          |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Source             | U.S. Department of Education (SRC-002)                                                         |
| Authority type     | regulation                                                                                     |
| Citation           | 34 CFR 99.10, 99.20-99.22                                                                      |
| Locator            | https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CFR-2025-title34-vol1/pdf/CFR-2025-title34-vol1-part99.pdf |
| Source version     | CFR annual edition revised 2025-07-01                                                          |
| Verified on        | 2026-08-19                                                                                     |
| Jurisdiction       | US-FEDERAL                                                                                     |
| Applicability      | APPLIES-AT-PILOT                                                                               |
| Trigger            | SSLS holds education-record data on behalf of a district.                                      |
| Control family     | PRIVACY                                                                                        |
| Control status     | SPECIFICATION-ONLY                                                                             |
| Evidence status    | NOT-PRODUCED                                                                                   |
| Owning route       | Deferred to the first persistence work package                                                 |
| Review requirement | LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED                                                                          |
| Review trigger     | First persistence design                                                                       |

**What the source states.** The rights run against the educational agency or institution. The regulation imposes no direct vendor workflow.

**Obligation.** Institutions must let parents and eligible students inspect records and request amendment of records believed inaccurate or misleading.

**SSLS interpretation.** Any SSLS record store must be able to produce a complete per-student export and support a correction path with provenance, or the district cannot meet its own duty.

**Current phase.** Not triggered.

**Future phase.** A hosting vendor must be able to surface and correct records so the district can honour inspection and amendment requests.

**Required control.** Per-subject record export and an auditable correction path with retained provenance.

**Current control.** Not built. The shared-object model defines record identity and relationships but no subject-access function exists.

**Evidence required.** Demonstrated export and correction workflow against synthetic data. Minimum method: Automated functional test plus reviewed walkthrough.

**Claim permitted.** SSLS may state that subject-access capability is specified but not implemented.

**Claim refused.** Supports FERPA access rights

**Note.** Recorded as a real design constraint on any future schema.

**What the source states.** Part 98 addresses the funded recipient. It contains no school-official style vendor exception.

**Obligation.** Recipients must provide notice and obtain consent or offer opt-out before administering surveys revealing protected categories, and must allow inspection of instruments.

**SSLS interpretation.** If SSLS ever builds a student-facing instrument, PPRA screening must occur at design time, not at deployment.

**Current phase.** Not triggered. No student-facing instrument exists.

**Future phase.** Any screener, family survey or behavioural instrument delivered to students would need to be assessed against the protected categories.

**Required control.** Design-time PPRA screening gate for any student-facing instrument.

**Current control.** None needed. No instrument capability exists.

**Evidence required.** Screening record for each instrument. Minimum method: Reviewed design record.

**Claim permitted.** No claim available.

**Claim refused.** PPRA compliant

**Note.** Recorded because multilingual-learner screening is a plausible future capability.

### OBL-004 — IDEA confidentiality and destruction of special-education PII

| Field              | Value                                                                                               |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Source             | U.S. Department of Education (SRC-004)                                                              |
| Authority type     | regulation                                                                                          |
| Citation           | 34 CFR 300.610, 300.622, 300.624                                                                    |
| Locator            | https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/34/300.610                                                     |
| Source version     | Part 300 as amended; currency conflicted                                                            |
| Verified on        | 2026-08-19                                                                                          |
| Jurisdiction       | US-FEDERAL                                                                                          |
| Applicability      | APPLIES-AT-PILOT                                                                                    |
| Trigger            | A state or local education agency shares real Part B personally identifiable information with SSLS. |
| Control family     | RETENTION & DELETION                                                                                |
| Control status     | MISSING                                                                                             |
| Evidence status    | NOT-PRODUCED                                                                                        |
| Owning route       | First persistence work package                                                                      |
| Review requirement | LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED                                                                               |
| Review trigger     | First special-education data model                                                                  |

**What the source states.** The duty is placed on the Secretary, state agencies and local agencies. The regulation does not bind vendors directly.

**Obligation.** Agencies must protect confidentiality of Part B personally identifiable information consistent with FERPA and must address destruction of information no longer needed for services, with notice to parents.

**SSLS interpretation.** Any special-education data model must carry a purge capability and a retention field from the first schema, because retrofitting deletion into a record system is not reliable.

**Current phase.** Not triggered.

**Future phase.** Special-education program data carries a destruction duty once information is no longer needed to provide services.

**Required control.** Retention field and verified purge capability on any special-education record type.

**Current control.** None. No persistence exists.

**Evidence required.** Purge execution evidence against synthetic records. Minimum method: Automated test with recorded artifact.

**Claim permitted.** None available.

**Claim refused.** IDEA compliant; SPED compliant

**Note.** Source currency is CONFLICTED (see SRC-004). Re-verification precedes any determination.

### OBL-005 — Verifiable parental consent for under-13 personal information

| Field              | Value                                                                                                                      |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Source             | Federal Trade Commission (SRC-006)                                                                                         |
| Authority type     | regulation                                                                                                                 |
| Citation           | 16 CFR 312.4, 312.5                                                                                                        |
| Locator            | https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2025-04-22/pdf/2025-05904.pdf                                                       |
| Source version     | Amended rule, effective 2025-06-23                                                                                         |
| Verified on        | 2026-08-19                                                                                                                 |
| Jurisdiction       | US-FEDERAL                                                                                                                 |
| Applicability      | CONDITIONAL                                                                                                                |
| Trigger            | SSLS operates a child-directed service or gains actual knowledge of collecting personal information from a child under 13. |
| Control family     | PRIVACY                                                                                                                    |
| Control status     | NOT-APPLICABLE                                                                                                             |
| Evidence status    | INAPPLICABLE                                                                                                               |
| Owning route       | Gate condition on any student-facing capability                                                                            |
| Review requirement | LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED                                                                                                      |
| Review trigger     | Any proposal for a student-facing surface                                                                                  |

**What the source states.** The rule addresses operators of child-directed or actual-knowledge services. The school-consent pathway comes from FTC guidance interpreting the rule.

**Obligation.** Operators must give notice and obtain verifiable parental consent before collecting, using or disclosing personal information from children under 13, with a school-authorised consent pathway recognised by FTC guidance for school-supported services.

**SSLS interpretation.** Any student-facing surface must be treated as child-directed by default until a documented age-gating analysis says otherwise.

**Current phase.** Not triggered. There is no child-facing surface and no personal information of any kind is collected.

**Future phase.** A student-facing feature would trigger the amended rule, whose general compliance date is 2026-04-22.

**Required control.** Consent architecture, age determination, and a documented child-directed analysis before student-facing launch.

**Current control.** No student-facing surface. Operator-only shell.

**Evidence required.** Child-directed determination record and consent-flow evidence. Minimum method: Reviewed determination record plus functional evidence.

**Claim permitted.** SSLS may state that no personal information is collected from anyone.

**Claim refused.** COPPA compliant; kid-safe; child-safe

**Note.** The nearest dated external trigger tracked by WP-038, and it is conditional, not automatic.

### OBL-006 — Written data retention and deletion policy for children's data

| Field              | Value                                                                |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Source             | Federal Trade Commission (SRC-006)                                   |
| Authority type     | regulation                                                           |
| Citation           | 16 CFR Part 312, 2025 amendments                                     |
| Locator            | https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2025-04-22/pdf/2025-05904.pdf |
| Source version     | Amended rule, effective 2025-06-23                                   |
| Verified on        | 2026-08-19                                                           |
| Jurisdiction       | US-FEDERAL                                                           |
| Applicability      | CONDITIONAL                                                          |
| Trigger            | Same trigger as OBL-005.                                             |
| Control family     | RETENTION & DELETION                                                 |
| Control status     | NOT-APPLICABLE                                                       |
| Evidence status    | INAPPLICABLE                                                         |
| Owning route       | First persistence work package                                       |
| Review requirement | PRIVACY REVIEW REQUIRED                                              |
| Review trigger     | First persistence design                                             |

**What the source states.** This is a new requirement added by the 2025 amendments.

**Obligation.** Operators must maintain a written retention policy, keep children's personal information only as long as reasonably necessary for the collection purpose, and delete it thereafter with reasonable disposal protection.

**SSLS interpretation.** Retention must be a declared field on any child-related record type rather than an operational habit.

**Current phase.** Not triggered.

**Future phase.** A written retention policy with defined deletion timing becomes mandatory, not optional.

**Required control.** Declared retention period per record type and evidenced deletion.

**Current control.** No data retained. Fixtures are compile-time constants.

**Evidence required.** Written policy artifact plus deletion execution evidence. Minimum method: Policy document plus automated deletion test.

**Claim permitted.** None available.

**Claim refused.** Meets COPPA retention requirements

### OBL-007 — Massachusetts student-record security and duty-limited vendor access

| Field              | Value                                                                                    |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Source             | Massachusetts Board of Elementary and Secondary Education (SRC-007)                      |
| Authority type     | regulation                                                                               |
| Citation           | 603 CMR 23.02, 23.05                                                                     |
| Locator            | https://www.doe.mass.edu/lawsregs/603cmr23.html                                          |
| Source version     | Amended 2026-01-27                                                                       |
| Verified on        | 2026-08-19                                                                               |
| Jurisdiction       | US-MA                                                                                    |
| Applicability      | APPLIES-AT-PILOT                                                                         |
| Trigger            | A Massachusetts district grants SSLS access to student records under a service contract. |
| Control family     | IDENTITY & ACCESS                                                                        |
| Control status     | SPECIFICATION-ONLY                                                                       |
| Evidence status    | NOT-PRODUCED                                                                             |
| Owning route       | First persistence and authentication work package                                        |
| Review requirement | LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED                                                                    |
| Review trigger     | First Massachusetts district agreement                                                   |

**What the source states.** The duty is placed on the principal, superintendent and school committee. The regulation does not create a direct vendor duty or penalty.

**Obligation.** Contracted service providers may be authorised school personnel with access limited to their duties, and the district must ensure computerised systems holding records are electronically secure.

**SSLS interpretation.** Duty-limited access is a schema and authorization requirement, not a contract clause alone. The SSLS authorization model already separates capacity, relationship, purpose and scope, which is the right shape for this.

**Current phase.** Not triggered.

**Future phase.** Access must be limited to what the vendor's duties require and computerised systems must be electronically secure.

**Required control.** Role and purpose scoped access enforced in the data layer, not only in the interface.

**Current control.** Authorization model specified in the shared-object architecture; no runtime enforcement exists because there is no data layer.

**Evidence required.** Enforced policy evidence at the data layer. Minimum method: Automated authorization tests plus reviewed policy definitions.

**Claim permitted.** SSLS may state that an authorization model is specified and unimplemented.

**Claim refused.** 603 CMR 23.00 compliant; Massachusetts student-records compliant

**Note.** Vendor exposure here is contractual, and the district holds the regulatory duty.

### OBL-008 — Massachusetts student-record destruction timelines

| Field              | Value                                                               |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Source             | Massachusetts Board of Elementary and Secondary Education (SRC-007) |
| Authority type     | regulation                                                          |
| Citation           | 603 CMR 23.06                                                       |
| Locator            | https://www.doe.mass.edu/lawsregs/603cmr23.html                     |
| Source version     | Amended 2026-01-27                                                  |
| Verified on        | 2026-08-19                                                          |
| Jurisdiction       | US-MA                                                               |
| Applicability      | APPLIES-AT-PILOT                                                    |
| Trigger            | SSLS stores Massachusetts student-record data for a district.       |
| Control family     | RETENTION & DELETION                                                |
| Control status     | MISSING                                                             |
| Evidence status    | NOT-PRODUCED                                                        |
| Owning route       | First persistence work package                                      |
| Review requirement | LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED                                               |
| Review trigger     | First persistence design                                            |

**What the source states.** 603 CMR 23.06 states the timelines. It addresses the district as record custodian.

**Obligation.** Sets differentiated destruction timelines for the transcript and the temporary record, and requires written notice before destruction.

**SSLS interpretation.** A single blanket retention setting cannot satisfy this. Record types must carry independent retention classes from the first schema.

**Current phase.** Not triggered.

**Future phase.** Transcript data is destroyable only after sixty years; the temporary record must be destroyed no later than seven years after transfer, graduation or withdrawal, with prior written notice.

**Required control.** Per-record-type retention class with a scheduled destruction path and pre-destruction notice hook.

**Current control.** None. No stored records.

**Evidence required.** Retention class definitions plus destruction execution evidence. Minimum method: Automated test plus reviewed schedule.

**Claim permitted.** None available.

**Claim refused.** Meets Massachusetts retention requirements

**Note.** This is the clearest example of an obligation that must shape schema design long before it applies.

### OBL-009 — Written comprehensive information security program

| Field              | Value                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Source             | Massachusetts Office of Consumer Affairs and Business Regulation (SRC-011)                                                                                                                                                       |
| Authority type     | regulation                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Citation           | 201 CMR 17.03                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Locator            | https://www.mass.gov/doc/201-cmr-17-standards-for-the-protection-of-personal-information-of-residents-of-the-commonwealth/download                                                                                               |
| Source version     | Current published edition                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Verified on        | 2026-08-19                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Jurisdiction       | US-MA                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Applicability      | CONDITIONAL                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Trigger            | SSLS owns, licenses, receives, stores, maintains, processes or otherwise has access to a Massachusetts resident's name combined with a Social Security number, driver's licence or state ID number, or financial account number. |
| Control family     | SECURITY                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Control status     | MISSING                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Evidence status    | NOT-PRODUCED                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Owning route       | Routed to the security work package; must precede any handling of narrow personal information                                                                                                                                    |
| Review requirement | SECURITY REVIEW REQUIRED                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Review trigger     | First handling of narrow personal information, including operator payroll or payment data                                                                                                                                        |

**What the source states.** 201 CMR 17.01 states the scope and 17.03 enumerates the program elements. Personal information is narrowly defined at 17.02.

**Obligation.** Requires a written information security program with designated responsibility, risk assessment, employee policy, access control on termination, service-provider oversight, monitoring, annual review and incident documentation.

**SSLS interpretation.** This is the most likely first binding security obligation on SSLS, and it may arrive through payroll or payment data rather than student data.

**Current phase.** Not triggered. No such data element is held, including for the operator.

**Future phase.** Triggers directly on the vendor, independently of any district contract. Employment or payment records could trigger it before any student data does.

**Required control.** A written information security program with the enumerated elements.

**Current control.** None. No written program exists. Technical controls exist in the evidence pipeline but they are not a program.

**Evidence required.** The written program plus annual review record. Minimum method: Document artifact with owner acceptance; automated evidence cannot satisfy this.

**Claim permitted.** SSLS may state that no Massachusetts-defined personal information is held.

**Claim refused.** 201 CMR 17 compliant; WISP in place

**Note.** Named as a gap because the trigger is closer than the student-data triggers.

| Applicability      | CONDITIONAL                                                                                                                        |

| Control family     | IDENTITY & ACCESS                                                                                                                  |
| Control status     | MISSING                                                                                                                            |
| Evidence status    | NOT-PRODUCED                                                                                                                       |
| Owning route       | First authentication work package                                                                                                  |
| Review requirement | SECURITY REVIEW REQUIRED                                                                                                           |
| Review trigger     | First authenticated deployment                                                                                                     |

**What the source states.** 17.04 enumerates the requirements. Subsections beyond (1) to (3) were not fully enumerated during WP-038 verification.

**Obligation.** Sets technical requirements including secure user authentication, access control, encryption in transit and on portable devices, monitoring and up-to-date protective software.

**SSLS interpretation.** These requirements shape the authentication design that SSLS does not yet have, so the design should be specified before it is needed.

**Current phase.** Not triggered.

**Future phase.** Requires secure authentication, access control, and encryption of personal information in transit across public networks and on portable devices.

**Required control.** Authenticated access with enforced transport encryption and device controls.

**Current control.** No authentication exists. The published surface is a public read-only prototype served over HTTPS with no accounts and no personal information.

**Evidence required.** Configuration evidence and authentication tests. Minimum method: Automated evidence plus reviewed configuration record.

**Claim permitted.** None available.

**Claim refused.** Encrypted and secure

**Note.** Clause-level enumeration of 17.04 is incomplete and recorded as a verification gap.

**Obligation.** A holder of another party's personal information must notify the owner promptly on discovering a breach of security.

**SSLS interpretation.** An incident response path with a defined notification clock must exist before SSLS holds any third-party data, because the clock starts at discovery, not at readiness.

**Current phase.** Not triggered.

**Future phase.** Requires notification to the owner or licensor as soon as practicable and without unreasonable delay.

**Required control.** Documented incident response procedure with a discovery-to-notification path.

**Current control.** None. No incident response procedure exists.

**Evidence required.** Written procedure plus a rehearsal record. Minimum method: Document artifact plus reviewed exercise record.

**Claim permitted.** None available.

**Claim refused.** Breach-ready; incident response in place

### OBL-013 — District web and mobile accessibility conformance to WCAG 2.1 AA

| Field              | Value                                                                                    |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Source             | U.S. Department of Justice (SRC-017)                                                     |
| Authority type     | regulation                                                                               |
| Citation           | 28 CFR 35.200(b)                                                                         |
| Locator            | https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2024/04/24/2024-07758                          |
| Source version     | Final rule 2024, dates extended by 2026 interim final rule                               |
| Verified on        | 2026-08-19                                                                               |
| Jurisdiction       | US-FEDERAL                                                                               |
| Applicability      | APPLIES-AT-PILOT                                                                         |
| Trigger            | A public entity uses SSLS as part of its web content or mobile services.                 |
| Control family     | ACCESSIBILITY                                                                            |
| Control status     | PARTIAL                                                                                  |
| Evidence status    | STALE                                                                                    |
| Owning route       | Accessibility validation work package                                                    |
| Review requirement | ACCESSIBILITY REVIEW REQUIRED                                                            |
| Review trigger     | Before any accessibility statement is published or any procurement response is submitted |

**What the source states.** The regulated party is the public entity. The rule does not regulate private vendors.

**Obligation.** Public entities must make web content and mobile applications conform to WCAG 2.1 Level AA, subject to listed exceptions and limited defences.

**SSLS interpretation.** Because the customer's duty is dated and non-negotiable, SSLS treats WCAG conformance as a product requirement now rather than a procurement surprise later. SSLS builds to WCAG 2.2 AA, which is a superset of the 2.1 AA criteria named in the rule.

**Current phase.** Not directly applicable. SSLS is not a public entity. The obligation reaches SSLS only through a district's own duty and its procurement terms.

**Future phase.** Districts must conform by 2027-04-26 for populations of fifty thousand or more, and 2028-04-26 for smaller populations and special district governments.

**Required control.** Verified conformance testing against the named criteria, with the internal target stated as a version.

**Current control.** ULW-AS-001 v1.3 internal standard applied across the shell, with automated axe-core checks in the test suite. Automated checks cover only part of the criteria set.

**Evidence required.** Manual and assistive-technology testing evidence in addition to automated checks. Minimum method: Automated scan plus documented manual testing. Independent audit is required before any external conformance statement.

**Claim permitted.** SSLS may state that it applies an internal accessibility standard and runs automated checks. It may not state conformance.

**Claim refused.** WCAG compliant; WCAG certified; ADA compliant; accessible

**Note.** Automated coverage is partial by nature. Recorded as PARTIAL rather than IMPLEMENTED for that reason.

**What the source states.** W3C states version status and conformance levels. W3C does not impose a legal duty.

**Obligation.** WCAG 2.2 is the current W3C Recommendation and its Level AA criteria form a superset of the WCAG 2.1 AA criteria named in ADA Title II and the HHS Section 504 rule.

**SSLS interpretation.** Targeting 2.2 AA satisfies the 2.1 AA criteria named in regulation and avoids a re-test cycle. This is an engineering decision, recorded as such, and it creates no conformance claim.

**Evidence required.** A recorded decision naming the target version and its relationship to ULW-AS-001. Minimum method: Owner decision record.

**Claim permitted.** SSLS may state which version it builds toward. It may not state that it meets it.

**Claim refused.** WCAG 2.2 AA conformant

**Note.** Raised as a decision candidate for the owner because the internal standard and the external version are not yet formally bound.

**Current control.** Claims Register CLM-001 to CLM-013 with recorded prohibited claims, plus a refused-claims boundary surface in the application.

**Evidence required.** The register plus review of published surfaces against it. Minimum method: Reviewed register with per-surface check.

**Claim permitted.** SSLS may state that it maintains a claims register and refuses specified claims.

**Claim refused.** AI-powered; AI-driven insights; intelligent recommendations

**Note.** This is one of the few obligations that applies right now to the current build.

### OBL-026 — Developer-directed AI design expectations

| Field              | Value                                                                    |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |

| Authority type     | official-guidance                                                        |
| Citation           | Designing for Education with AI: An Essential Guide for Developers       |
| Locator            | https://www.ed.gov/sites/ed/files/documents/ai-report/ai-report.pdf      |
| Source version     | 2023 report with 2024 developer guide                                    |
| Verified on        | 2026-08-19                                                               |
| Jurisdiction       | US-FEDERAL                                                               |
| Applicability      | REFERENCE                                                                |
| Trigger            | Any AI capability design.                                                |
| Control family     | HUMAN REVIEW                                                             |
| Control status     | SPECIFICATION-ONLY                                                       |
| Evidence status    | INAPPLICABLE                                                             |
| Owning route       | Gate condition on any AI capability                                      |
| Review requirement | EDUCATION POLICY REVIEW REQUIRED                                         |
| Review trigger     | Any proposed AI capability                                               |

**What the source states.** The Department states the guidance is non-regulatory and that examples are not endorsements.

**Obligation.** Non-regulatory recommendations for developers on evidence, transparency, human oversight and equity in educational AI.

**SSLS interpretation.** Its emphasis on evidence-bound output and human review matches the SSLS rule that AI output must be reviewable and never autonomously decide.

**Current phase.** Reference. Explicitly non-regulatory.

**Future phase.** Would inform design review for any AI capability.

**Required control.** Human review requirement on any AI-produced output.

**Current control.** Encoded as a refusal rule: no autonomous high-impact decisions, and no AI features in this phase.

**Evidence required.** Design record per AI feature. Minimum method: Reviewed design record.

**Claim permitted.** None available.

**Claim refused.** Department of Education endorsed; ED aligned

| Citation           | OneRoster v1.2                                                                     |
| Locator            | https://www.1edtech.org/standards/oneroster                                        |
| Source version     | 1.2                                                                                |
| Verified on        | 2026-08-19                                                                         |
| Jurisdiction       | NOT-JURISDICTIONAL                                                                 |
| Applicability      | APPLIES-AT-PILOT                                                                   |
| Trigger            | A district needs to sync students, organisations, classes or enrolments into SSLS. |
| Control family     | INTEROPERABILITY                                                                   |
| Control status     | SPECIFICATION-ONLY                                                                 |
| Evidence status    | NOT-PRODUCED                                                                       |
| Owning route       | First ingestion work package                                                       |
| Review requirement | none recorded                                                                      |
| Review trigger     | First ingestion design                                                             |

**What the source states.** 1EdTech publishes the specification and operates the certification programme.

**Obligation.** Standardises exchange of roster, course and grade data through CSV bulk and REST modes. Certification is granted only after passing the test suite.

**SSLS interpretation.** Roster shape should constrain the shared-object student model now, so that a later adapter is a mapping rather than a migration.

**Current phase.** Not triggered. No ingestion path exists.

**Future phase.** Required in practice for any district pilot that must load a real roster.

**Required control.** Student and enrolment models compatible with OneRoster entities.

**Current control.** Shared-object model defines student-adjacent object types but no OneRoster mapping exists.

**Evidence required.** Mapping document plus certification if conformance is ever claimed. Minimum method: 1EdTech certification for any conformance statement; internal mapping evidence otherwise.

**Claim permitted.** SSLS may state that no roster integration exists.

**Claim refused.** OneRoster conformant; OneRoster certified; OneRoster compatible

**Note.** Implementing a specification informally is not certified conformance.

**What the source states.** These are private contract templates, not law.

**SSLS interpretation.** The agreement, not the regulation, is what will actually bind SSLS first. Preparing for it is a product requirement, not a legal one.

### OBL-032 — Accuracy of public claims on the published prototype

| Field              | Value                                                   |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| Source             | Massachusetts Office of the Attorney General (SRC-014)  |
| Authority type     | official-guidance                                       |
| Citation           | AGO AI Advisory; M.G.L. c. 93A as referenced therein    |
| Locator            | https://www.mass.gov/doc/ago-ai-advisory-41624/download |
| Source version     | 2024-04-16                                              |
| Verified on        | 2026-08-19                                              |
| Jurisdiction       | US-MA                                                   |
| Applicability      | APPLIES-NOW                                             |
| Trigger            | A public surface exists at a reachable URL.             |
| Control family     | CLAIMS / TRANSPARENCY                                   |
| Control status     | IMPLEMENTED                                             |
| Evidence status    | CURRENT                                                 |
| Owning route       | WP-037 publication boundary; maintained continuously    |
| Review requirement | none recorded                                           |
| Review trigger     | Every publication                                       |

**What the source states.** The advisory states that existing consumer protection law applies. It does not enumerate product wording.

**Obligation.** Consumer protection law applies to representations made about a product, including capability, security, privacy and compliance statements.

**SSLS interpretation.** Publication is not release, and the published surface must say so. Every status shown must be traceable to a recorded fact.

**Current phase.** Applies now. A public prototype is published and reachable.

**Future phase.** Applies with greater consequence as commercial intent becomes explicit.

**Required control.** Publication boundary statement plus traceable status rendering.

**Current control.** PUBLIC PROTOTYPE boundary recorded in WP-037, refused-claims surface in the application, and authority never derived from implementation status.

**Evidence required.** Reachability evidence plus surface review against the claims register. Minimum method: Recorded evidence plus human review.

**Claim permitted.** SSLS may describe the published surface as a public prototype that is not a release.

**Claim refused.** Production ready; district ready; live product

### OBL-033 — Zero personal data on the current surface

| Field              | Value                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Source             | Massachusetts Office of Consumer Affairs and Business Regulation (SRC-011)                                                         |
| Authority type     | regulation                                                                                                                         |
| Citation           | 201 CMR 17.01 scope                                                                                                                |
| Locator            | https://www.mass.gov/doc/201-cmr-17-standards-for-the-protection-of-personal-information-of-residents-of-the-commonwealth/download |
| Source version     | Current published edition                                                                                                          |
| Verified on        | 2026-08-19                                                                                                                         |
| Jurisdiction       | US-MA                                                                                                                              |
| Applicability      | APPLIES-NOW                                                                                                                        |
| Trigger            | The scope test is continuous: the obligation attaches the moment personal information is received.                                 |
| Control family     | DATA MINIMIZATION                                                                                                                  |
| Control status     | IMPLEMENTED                                                                                                                        |
| Evidence status    | CURRENT                                                                                                                            |
| Owning route       | WP-038 verification; maintained continuously                                                                                       |
| Review requirement | none recorded                                                                                                                      |
| Review trigger     | Any added form, account, analytics or third-party script                                                                           |

**What the source states.** 17.01 states the scope. It does not describe web surfaces specifically.

**Obligation.** The regulation attaches to any person that receives, stores, maintains, processes or has access to personal information about a Massachusetts resident.

**SSLS interpretation.** Keeping the collection surface empty is the cheapest available control, and it must be verified rather than assumed.

**Current phase.** Applies now as a boundary to hold, not as a duty being discharged. The current surface collects nothing.

**Future phase.** The moment any form, account or analytics capture is added, OBL-009 to OBL-012 attach.

**Required control.** Verified absence of collection: no accounts, no forms that transmit, no analytics, no third-party trackers.

**Current control.** Verified at WP-038: no authentication, no submitting forms, no analytics or tracking scripts, no third-party data calls. One first-party sidebar preference cookie is set by the interface. Platform error reporting is invoked only if the host injects it.

**Evidence required.** Repeatable scan of the source tree for collection paths. Minimum method: Automated boundary scan plus code review.

**Claim permitted.** SSLS may state that the current surface collects no personal information and sets one first-party preference cookie.

**Claim refused.** Privacy compliant; no cookies; no tracking of any kind

**Note.** The sidebar preference cookie is recorded rather than omitted, because a no-cookies claim would be inaccurate.

| Citation           | CIS Controls v8.1, Control 16                                                |
| Locator            | https://www.cisecurity.org/controls/v8-1                                     |
| Source version     | 8.1                                                                          |
| Verified on        | 2026-08-19                                                                   |
| Jurisdiction       | NOT-JURISDICTIONAL                                                           |
| Applicability      | APPLIES-NOW                                                                  |
| Trigger            | SSLS maintains a repository that is the authorised software source of truth. |
| Control family     | GOVERNANCE                                                                   |
| Control status     | PARTIAL                                                                      |
| Evidence status    | NOT-PRODUCED                                                                 |
| Owning route       | FND-012 remains open                                                         |
| Review requirement | none recorded                                                                |
| Review trigger     | Any claim about change control                                               |

**What the source states.** CIS publishes voluntary safeguards.

**Obligation.** Recommends controlled change processes for application software, including review and enforcement of protections.

**SSLS interpretation.** A workflow that exists is not an enforcement that is configured. The distinction is already recorded as FND-012.

**Current phase.** Applies now as an internal practice.

**Future phase.** Becomes an evidence question in any security review.

**Required control.** Verified branch protection requiring the evidence and binding checks to pass.

**Current control.** CI workflows exist. Branch-protection enforcement is not verified.

**Evidence required.** Repository settings evidence. Minimum method: Configuration evidence from the hosting platform.

**Claim permitted.** SSLS may state that CI workflows exist and that enforcement is unverified.

**Claim refused.** Enforced change control; protected main branch

**Note.** Carried from WP-037 rather than restated as a new finding.
